name: Carrd
tagline: Simple one-page website builder for landing pages and profiles

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Pro Standard listed at $19/year, equivalent to about $1.58/month.

verdictSummary: A one-page static site generator with forms and custom domains is absolutely vibecodable; Carrd's price is so low that DIY only makes sense for control or learning.
coreLoopDIY: Generate/edit a single-page HTML site from blocks, host it, attach a domain, and optionally send forms to email/webhook.
whatYouLose: not having to think about hosting
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because the product costs almost nothing and removes all hosting/domain friction.

priorArt.name: GrapesJS
priorArt.desc: Open-source web builder library; enough to build a simple Carrd-like editor.

alternatives.name: Mobirise AI
alternatives.desc: Three generated and exportable sites a month for free; the templates retain a faint Bootstrap aftertaste.

alternatives.name: Plasmic
alternatives.desc: A custom-domain visual site on the free plan; comically overpowered for a one-page profile and branded accordingly.

alternatives.name: Silex
alternatives.desc: A visual one-page builder that exports plain HTML and costs nothing; publishing begins with a GitLab login.

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: Three hosted funnels and a custom domain free; perfect when the one-page site is secretly collecting leads.

alternatives.name: Webstudio
alternatives.desc: Far more CSS control than Carrd and far more self-hosting responsibility.

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A library for creating builders, not the one-page builder a normal person came to install.

notes: To be fair, Carrd is famously cheap. But you have Claude Code; you don't need a site builder at all.
prompt:
Build me a one-page personal site to replace Carrd. Requirements:

- One elegant single-page site from a content.json file: name, headline, short
  about paragraph, avatar, social links, and an optional list of projects with
  title + description + URL. Editing the JSON is the CMS.
- Design it properly: strong typographic hierarchy, generous whitespace, one
  accent color set via a CSS variable, dark mode via prefers-color-scheme,
  tasteful hover states. It should look designed, not templated.
- A working contact form with no third-party service: POST to a tiny endpoint
  that appends to messages.log and returns an inline thank-you. Honeypot field
  for bots.
- Perfect Lighthouse scores: inline the CSS, no frameworks, no webfonts unless
  self-hosted, proper OG tags + generated OG image.
- Static HTML + one small server file for the form. Deploy instructions for
  any VPS or static host + serverless form alternative.
